title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck sets out to build a theory of 'Albanese equivalence' of algebraic cycles. The margin note is a reminder to consult Weil's 'Critères d'équivalence en géométrie algébrique' (Math. Ann. 1954).

Definition 1.1. Let X be smooth (the word 'projective' is crossed out) over a field k, and z a cycle on X. Then z is Albanese-equivalent to 0 if there exist:
- a smooth connected (projective) k-scheme T,
- a 0-cycle 𝔄 on T of degree 0 with S_T(𝔄)=0, i.e. 𝔄 lies in the Albanese kernel T(T) = ker(alb: CH_0(T)_0 → Alb_T(k)),
- a cycle Z on X×T (a correspondence)
such that Z(𝔄) = pr_{X*}(Z·pr_T^*𝔄) is defined and equals z.
Compare algebraic equivalence, where 𝔄 is only required to have degree 0. Here 𝔄 must also die in the Albanese. If T is restricted to curves the condition forces 𝔄 ~_rat 0, so one recovers rational equivalence. Since T may have any dimension, and the Albanese kernel of a surface can be huge (Mumford), the relation sits strictly between rational and algebraic equivalence.

Proposition 1.2, continued on the next page:
(i) Such cycles form a subgroup N*(X) ⊂ Cyc*(X) containing the cycles linearly (= rationally) equivalent to 0. So N is determined by its image N'*(X) in A*(X) = the Chow ring, and Cyc/N ≅ A*/N'.
(ii) N' is an ideal, so A'*(X) = CH*(X)/N'*(X) is a ring.
(iii) f^* preserves N' for morphisms of smooth quasi-projective varieties.
(iv) f_* preserves N' for proper f.
(v) Albanese equivalence implies algebraic equivalence, so one can speak of algebraically trivial classes in A'.
In short, Albanese equivalence is an adequate equivalence relation.

The proofs are formal consequences of the composition of correspondences:
- sums: take T×T' with 𝔄×t'_0 + t_0×𝔄';
- products and the ideal property: ξ·η = (Z·(η×T))(𝔄) by the projection formula;
- f^*, f_*: compose Z with the graph of f.

Consequences (not written on the page but immediate):
- On 0-cycles, N = the Albanese kernel of X. Take T = X and Z = Δ for one inclusion; functoriality of Alb under correspondences gives the other.
- On divisors, N = rational equivalence, because any correspondence induces Alb_T → Pic^0_X.
- In general codimension, N ⊂ the kernel of any regular homomorphism to an abelian variety (Murre's algebraic representative).
The aim is evidently to have a ring A' on which algebraic-equivalence classes carry abelian-variety structure, between Chow groups and cycles modulo algebraic equivalence. This is input for the standard-conjecture / motive programme of this dossier.
errors: Notational clash: Z denotes both the cycle on X and the correspondence on X×T; the target is written lowercase z at the end. Intended: z = Z(𝔄).

The machine transcription's 'contenant les gr. des cycles num. équiv. à 0' would be mathematically wrong, since Albanese ⊂ algebraic ⊂ numerical. The image reads 'lin. équiv.' (linear/rational equivalence), and A*(X) is the ring of classes 'à équiv. linéaire près', i.e. the Chow ring. With that reading the statement is correct.

'Z(𝔄) défini' tacitly requires a moving lemma, or Fulton-style refined intersection, for the correspondence action; for quasi-projective (non-projective) X this needs care, and the word 'projectif' is hesitantly crossed out and re-bracketed.

Not justified on this page: that the relation is independent of choices and closed under sums requires T×T' and base points, which is standard but slightly delicate when k is not algebraically closed (existence of rational points on T).

ideas.what: Albanese equivalence of cycles: images under correspondences of degree-0 zero-cycles in the Albanese kernel of a smooth parameter variety
ideas.modern_name: Adequate equivalence relation generated by the Albanese kernel; close to step F^2 of S. Saito / Jannsen correspondence-defined filtrations, and contained in the kernel of Murre's algebraic representatives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Albanese kernel: Bloch, Mumford (1968-75); correspondence-defined filtrations: H. Saito (1979), S. Saito (1996), Jannsen (1994); algebraic representatives: Murre (1983-85)
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in SGA/EGA as far as I know; Grothendieck mentions related themes only informally (Standard conjectures, 1969)

ideas.what: Albanese equivalence is adequate: subgroup, ideal, stable under f^* and f_*, giving a ring A'*(X) = CH*/N'
ideas.modern_name: Adequate equivalence relation in the sense of Samuel; intermediate Chow-type ring between CH* and CH*/alg
ideas.usually_credited_to: Samuel (1958) for adequate relations in general

ideas.what: Albanese equivalence ⇒ algebraic equivalence, so 'algebraically trivial' makes sense in A'

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, c. 1965-71, a correspondence-generated adequate equivalence relation built from Albanese kernels of arbitrary parameter varieties, i.e. a 'second step' filtration on Chow groups. This predates Bloch's work on Albanese kernels and the S. Saito / Jannsen / Murre correspondence-defined filtrations (F^2 = images of Albanese kernels under correspondences). It is not usually credited to him.
missed.quote: On dit que z est alb-équiv. à 0, si on peut trouver un schéma [projectif] lisse connexe T sur k, un cycle 𝔄 sur T, et un cycle Z sur X×T, tels que (i) 𝔄 est de degré 0 et S_γ(𝔄)=0 (ii) Z(𝔄) est défini et égal à z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an early, purely geometric definition of the F^2-type step of the conjectural Bloch–Beilinson/Murre filtration on general CH^p, as an adequate relation with a ring quotient A'. The open question it implicitly poses — whether N' equals the kernel of Murre's algebraic representative on algebraically trivial cycles — is still subtle. It is of historical interest; the mathematics is likely known to specialists in some form.

missed.claim: The programme of studying the ring A'*(X) = CH/Albanese-equivalence, and algebraically trivial classes therein, as an object of the theory of motives is begun but its continuation is unknown here.
missed.quote: (Donc on peut parler d'éléments de A'^*(X) alg. équiv. à 0 !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Natural question: is A'^*_{alg}(X) representable by an abelian variety (a strengthening of Murre's algebraic representatives)? Relevant to Murre's conjectures and the Bloch conjecture.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, unpublished definition by Grothendieck of an adequate 'Albanese equivalence' between rational and algebraic equivalence, anticipating later correspondence-defined filtrations (Bloch, S. Saito, Murre). The proofs are formal and the notion is close to things later in the literature, so it is historically notable rather than mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: 'contenant les gr. des cycles num. équiv. à 0' should read 'contenant le gr. des cycles lin. équiv. à 0' (linear equivalence).
'défini par les classes à équiv. numérique près' should read 'défini par les classes à équiv. linéaire près': A*(X) is the Chow ring.
'S_γ(𝔄)' is probably S_T(𝔄), the summation (Albanese) map of T.
Final 'égal à z': the cycle on X is lowercase z, distinct from the correspondence Z on X×T.
